lessons.title: Contact Center webhooks
lessons.summary: Subscriptions want an HTTPS URL with no query string. The signature header is X-WebexCC-Signature, HMAC-SHA256. Events follow CloudEvents. Do not use webhooks as your only copy of the data.
objectives: Require HTTPS without query parameters
Verify X-WebexCC-Signature
Keep a second way to read the data

diagram.caption: Verify the signature, then still reconcile.

flow.title: A contact event hits your server

steps.label: Register a destinationUrl
steps.detail: The contact center webhooks guide requires HTTPS. Query parameters on that URL are not accepted.

steps.label: POST the event
steps.detail: The body is a CloudEvent. Parse the raw bytes for the signature before you re-serialize JSON.
steps.inspect: Do not trust a proxy that rewrites the body

steps.label: Check X-WebexCC-Signature
steps.detail: HMAC-SHA256 with the secret. Compare in constant time.
steps.inspect: This is not the messaging HMAC-SHA1 header

steps.label: Reconcile
steps.detail: The guide says not to rely solely on webhooks. Use the search or task APIs when an event may have been missed.

paragraphs: Messaging webhooks use X-Spark-Signature as HMAC-SHA1 when you supply a secret, and may also send X-Webex-Signature as HMAC-SHA256 or HMAC-SHA512.
Contact center subscriptions use X-WebexCC-Signature. Mixing the headers fails verification.
If your listener is down, you need another way to notice. The webhooks guide is explicit that webhooks are not the only source you should trust.
Answer with a 2xx when you accept the event, or the delivery is not successful.

lessons.title: GraphQL search limits
lessons.summary: The search API is GraphQL, regional, and bounded. The US example host is not every region. The window and the history floor are part of the contract.
objectives: Use the regional host
Pass from and to as epoch milliseconds
Respect the 365-day window and the 36-month floor

diagram.caption: Ask for a window the API allows.

steps.label: Ask for cjp:config or cjp:config_read
steps.detail: The search reference lists those scopes. A messaging token with no contact center scope will not do.
steps.inspect: Least privilege: read if you only search

steps.label: Use the region
steps.detail: The example host api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com is the US1 example. Other regions have their own hosts. Do not hardcode US1 for a European tenant.
steps.inspect: The API index says the host is regional

steps.label: from and to in epoch milliseconds
steps.detail: from must not be older than 36 months. The window cannot exceed 365 days.
steps.inspect: Split a long history into windows

steps.label: Fill what a missed event skipped
steps.detail: Search is one way to reconcile. It is not a license to ignore the window.

paragraphs: Epoch milliseconds, not seconds. A 365-day maximum window. from no older than 36 months. Those limits are from the search reference this lab cites.
If the live page changes the numbers, the page wins. The lesson states them so you know what to look for.
It is not the messaging REST API and not the xAPI command endpoint.
The contact center API overview is the index. Getting started for general Webex tokens is a different page and is not the contact center guide.
